mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced discount rates and increased liquidity in the financial system.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.5% in a 3-month window, it signals a deteriorating labor market that triggers risk-off sentiment, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5% (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in CPIAUCSL (indicating a shift from monetary easing to tightening while inflation rises) signals a 'transitory inflation' phase that increases equity risk premiums, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decline > 0.2% and CPIAUCSL rise > 0.3% in the last 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition (FEDFUNDS decline > 0.2% and CPIAUCSL rise > 0.3% in last 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 (index 2017=100) signals strong economic activity that reduces the risk of recession, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 105 (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.5% signals robust economic growth, which reduces the probability of a recession and increases equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1000 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market that increases the risk of a recession, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 1000 (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth > 2.5% and unemployment rate < 5%), rising retail sales (RSAFS) above 450,000 million dollars signals strong consumer demand that supports equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS > 450,000 and the regime condition (GDP growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 5%) holds (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (index 2017=100), it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector that increases the risk of a recession, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns vs baseline).
